about: Born, Not Made, simplified version after the sketch of 21 November 2026. Frame: x toward the opening, y port, z up, meters; origin on the docking plane, on the inner floor (the tank floor is 3 mm lower).

h2s.t: Bambu Lab H2S, build volume 340 x 320 x 340 mm

dex.t: Rotrics DexArm specification page (opened 22 Nov 2026): payload 500 g max (400 g in the Teach and Pneumatic section), reach 380 mm (Teach and Pneumatic section), weight 2.4 kg, repeatability 0.05 mm, base plus or minus 110, joint 1 0 to 110, joint 2 0 to 85 degrees

ds.t: Smooth-On Dragon Skin 10 NV technical bulletin: 100 % modulus 27 psi, elongation at break 663 %, specific gravity 1.07

kres.t: B. Kresling, Natural twist buckling in shells, Proc. 6th Int. Conf. on Computation of Shell and Spatial Structures, IASS-IACM 2008, Ithaca

cai.t: J. Cai, X. Deng, Y. Zhou, J. Feng, Y. Tu, Bistable behavior of the cylindrical origami structure with Kresling pattern, J. Mech. Des. 137(6) 061406, 2015

reid.t: A. Reid, F. Lechenault, S. Rica, M. Adda-Bedia, Geometry and design of origami bellows with tunable response, Phys. Rev. E 95, 013002, 2017

pump.t: Mini submersible pump, DC 3 to 5 V (reseller page for the pump class of the AITIAO pump the artist owns; no primary page exists)

tank.t: Glass tank made to order, 1750 x 600 x 600 mm, 15 mm low iron glass

magnet.t: Adafruit 3872, 5 V electromagnet: 20 mm across, 15 mm tall, 0.22 A, 2.5 kg holding force, 22.7 g

gelpump.t: Adafruit 3910, peristaltic liquid pump: 5 to 6 V, up to 100 mL per minute, 104 g (stands outside the tank, at the gel bottle)

carbopol.t: T. Bhattacharjee et al., Writing in the granular gel medium, Sci. Adv. 1(8), e1500655, 2015: 0.2 percent (w/v) Carbopol ETD 2020, yield stress 9 Pa, shear modulus 64 Pa; 0.05 to 1 percent explored

mag.t: K&J Magnetics DC2-N52 disc magnet, 19.05 x 3.17 mm, 12.08 lb pull on a steel plate

grow.case_text: The newborn leaves uniformly partly filled, at 26 percent of the grown gas volume, with the pleats still visible, and grows outside past the printed full size, the skin stretching like a balloon (the stretch goes from 1.07 to 1.66; past the limit point 1.38 the pressure falls as the body inflates, so even growth is assumed). The release over the lower lip is drawn as a prescribed path; its dynamics are not modeled.

kit.name: Encapsulated kit, water pump for the jet, air pump for growth

parts.name: AITIAO 3 to 5 V micro submersible pump, 42.6 x 23.9 x 22.7 mm (the pump the artist owns)
Water held in the pump chamber and the tubes
Silicone tube stubs (one intake, one jet) and wiring
Hand cast encapsulation, Dragon Skin 10 NV, with three feet
Air pump, small diaphragm class, about 30 x 20 x 15 mm (assumed catalogue class, not a cited product)

Snorkel tube to the top of the body, check valve and pocket filler; the air pump takes the place of the earlier growth cell within the same pocket, so the kit envelope and mass are unchanged (estimate)
Steel disk for the electromagnet, 20 x 1 mm

stages.name: Dock in the water
stages.text: Water in the tank and gel in both parts from the first frame. The tail slides forward and docks from behind, its gel face against the gel face of the head; the last 10 mm slowly. Three disc magnets press the docking ring onto a soft cord.

stages.name: Unfold, top up
stages.text: The arm unfolds. The gel is already in (3.57 L); the line on the arm only tops up the 25 mL that left with the last newborn.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The electromagnet picks the electronics kit once, from its place in the tail, and carries the kit through the gel to the print seat, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change in the tail: holder off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release). The needle travels in the gel to the print.

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the folded newborn around the kit: 121 m of bead, 0.23 L of Dragon Skin 10 NV.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, holder on.

stages.name: Air in, nose up
stages.text: The ball needle enters the valve. Air pushes the trapped gel out of the folds, the newborn floats up in the gel, and the arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises above the lip.

stages.name: Push while inflating
stages.text: The arm steers the tail end from above and pushes it forward to the edge of its reach (the valve at 224 mm from the arm axis, 172 mm high); the front of the newborn passes the mouth and opens, the rear stays in the gel inside the head. No contractions.

stages.name: Hold and fill
stages.text: The arm holds, the newborn fills to 60 percent of its full gas volume on purpose and leaves partly filled; the needle lets go.

stages.name: Hold
stages.text: The holder holds the partly filled newborn at the edge of its reach, then the needle lets go.

stages.name: Release, float
stages.text: Release, drawn, not simulated: at each step of a drawn forward motion the newborn takes its pose of least energy (weight against buoyancy in the gel and the water) with its lowest contact 3 mm clear of the floor: it settles onto the gel, rests on the ramp and is carried up it (the tail end rises 119 mm), tips over the lower lip and settles into the water. What drives the slide is not modeled. Then it floats free.

stages.name: Swim and grow
stages.text: The newborn leaves folded and wrinkled, and the pleats open as the body fills while the newborn swims straight ahead on one slow steady jet (3 percent duty). Floating at the surface, the newborn takes in air above the waterline through a short snorkel at the top of the body, and the small air pump in the kit fills the body from 26 to 100 percent of the grown volume (7.1 to 28.0 L). Past the printed full size the silicone skin stretches on like a balloon, to 1.66 times its unfolded size, until the body is smooth, round and 566 x 328 mm.

stages.name: Grown
stages.text: Grown, the newborn has the form of the parent body in small, about as large as the head. The growth happened during the swim (see Swim and grow); here the newborn comes to rest, straight ahead of the mouth.

notes: The tank is full and the gel is in from the start: each part holds its own gel at the open docking face, level with the water. The tail slides forward along the floor and docks from behind; the two gel faces meet and the water between them is squeezed out. Three magnets press the seam onto its cord.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, over the gel. The base does not move.
The line on the arm tops up the gel that left with the last newborn (25 mL); no filling, the gel stays from birth to birth.
The bare arm folds back into the tail.
The bare arm turns to the holder: an electromagnet and a ball needle on a saddle beside the arm.
The quick release slides onto the holder and clicks.
The holder leaves its saddle sideways, its needle in the gel, and turns to the kit, which waits in the gel in front of the arm.
The magnet lands on the steel disk of the kit.
Magnet on: the magnet holds the kit by the steel disk.
The kit is carried forward through the gel, across the seam, to the print seat.
The kit goes down onto the three seat bumps.
Magnet off: the kit stays on the seat, held by the gel; the holder lifts clear.
Tool change in the tail: the holder comes back through the gel.
The holder slides sideways onto its saddle.
The pin on the saddle presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm turns to the print needle on the other side.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle leaves its saddle sideways, its tip in the gel.
The needle moves forward through the gel, across the seam, to the print.
The folded newborn is printed around the kit, layer by layer, in clear silicone.
The silicone cures in the gel (75 minutes at room temperature). The print needle goes back over the print to its saddle in the tail.
The holder is back on the arm: the ball needle beside the magnet now carries the air.
The holder moves forward to the newborn.
The ball needle goes to the valve on the tail end of the newborn.
Air at 450 Pa pushes the gel out of the folds through the vent in the nose; the drained newborn rises 30 mm and floats in the gel.
The needle presses the tail end down in the gel: the nose rises above the lip of the opening.

Push while inflating: the arm pushes the tail end forward to the edge of its reach while air comes in through the ball needle; the front stories pass the mouth and open, the rear stories stay inside the head, partly folded.
At full reach the arm holds the needle in the valve and fills the newborn to 60 percent of its full gas volume, on purpose: full, the body might not pass the mouth. The creases stay partly visible.
The holder keeps the needle in the valve at the edge of its reach while the gas settles; then the needle lets go.

Release, drawn, not simulated: the needle lets go; the newborn settles onto the gel and the floor of the head, slides up the ramp of the floor resting on it, tips over the lower lip and settles into the water. What drives the slide is not modeled.
Reload for the next birth: the holder leaves its saddle sideways and slides the next kit along the two rails into the pick pocket. The magazine held three kits; two are left.
The newborn floats free in front of the mouth, folded and wrinkled (26 percent of the grown gas volume); the arm parks the holder and folds back into the tail.

The water pump in the kit pushes one slow steady jet out behind while the air pump takes in air above the waterline and fills the body: the newborn swims straight ahead and grows while swimming, the skin stretching beyond the printed size.
Grown: the newborn rests at the end of the straight swim, smooth and round, the form of the parent body in small.

checks.name: Tail in one print on the H2S: 335 x 314 x 336 mm, of 340 x 320 x 340
Head 396 x 314 x 336 mm, the length of the double wall head: longer than the 340 mm bed of the H2S, so it needs a larger printer or a split, which is not shown
Everything for the tools is behind the docking plane: the saddles, the two modules and the kit store end 4 mm behind the plane. Only the stems and the kit stand in the gel, which runs across the seam

No tool crosses a wall: close to its base the arm holds the needle tip at most 18 mm high (at 150 mm from the axis), so the print needle and the holder hang with their stems in the gel and travel in the gel to the print; a wall at the docking plane could be only 17 mm tall
Folded arm ends 50 mm behind the docking plane; tower top 11 mm under the tail roof
The print needle reaches all 1849 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges

Before docking, alone in 93.8 mm of water with its own gel, the tail weighs 6.6 kg against 6.0 kg of buoyancy (lightest case: after the last of the births, the store empty): the 5 mm steel plate under the arm base is the only ballast

Before docking, alone in the water with its own gel, the head weighs 4.22 kg against 2.76 kg of buoyancy, no ballast block (gel and water have nearly the same density, so only the shell counts: 1468 g net). Docked and with the print in: 4.1 kg against 2.8 kg

The gel is never taken out under water: emptied, the docked parent body would lift (7.7 kg against 8.7 kg of buoyancy). With water instead of gel the head would still sink (shell 1.62 kg, buoyancy 1.27 kg)

Gel and water from the first frame. Before docking each part holds its gel at the open docking face: the gel stands 0.0 mm above the water (0.0 Pa), the density difference adds 1.8 Pa at the floor; 1.8 Pa against an assumed yield stress of 25 Pa (Carbopol about 0.4 percent, to be measured; 0.2 percent gives 9 Pa, Bhattacharjee 2015)

Docking into the gel: the two gel faces (95 cm2) close at 1 mm per second over the last 10 mm; the water between them is squeezed out up to the surface down to a film of about 0.11 mm, so about 1 mL of water stay in 3.57 L of gel (0.03 percent, estimate)

The open gel faces before docking: below the yield stress the gel does not flow; ions of the neutralizer diffuse into the water about 4 mm in an hour and 21 mm in a day (D = 1.3e-9 m2/s), where the gel may soften. Dock within the hour; needs a bench test

Wet seam, water outside and gel inside: with the print in, the gel side is higher by 92 Pa at the floor and 91 Pa at the waterline, so water cannot enter at any height; gel does not pass a gap under 2.2 mm through the 4 mm cord seat, the cord closes it. Before the print the gel and the water stand level and the difference is 2 Pa
The lip is 52 mm above the water and 43.0 mm above the gel; the ridge in front of the arm base stands 13 mm above the water, so the dry part of the tail stays dry while the tail is apart

The gel stays in the box between births: 3.57 L, about 25 mL leave with each newborn (0.7 percent), topped up through the arm. The volume is what the lower line of the double wall head gives, target changed to at most 3.6 L
The lip is 43 mm above the gel surface; the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm, and the folded print has already raised the level before the push
The store lies behind the arm, clear of it: nearest to the shell 4.5 mm, nearest to the space the arm sweeps 3.7 mm. Nothing beside the arm base, no bulkhead, no ballast block

Births per fill of the store: 1 (the silicone sets it; the store is refilled between visits). Kits: 3 (the magazine holds one kit in the pick pocket and one in each side pocket; near its base the arm holds a tool within 7 mm of one height, so kits cannot be stacked, and the gel slot between the ridge and the docking plane is 62 mm deep). Silicone: 1. Energy: 1. Gel top ups: 1. The shorter tail holds the store for one birth

Energy for 1 cycles: 23 Wh each (the gel pump now included); the battery (nine 18650 cells, 3S3P) holds 38 Wh: margin 1.63 for 1 cycles. The inflator runs on a battery of its own (USB, recharged between visits)
Silicone for 1 newborns: the two cartridges hold 255 mL, each newborn takes 226 mL (226 mL for 1, margin 1.13)
Gel top up for 1 births: the reservoir holds 27 mL, each birth takes 25 mL; the pump (Adafruit 3910) gives up to 100 mL per minute through the line on the arm

Kit reload, checked frame by frame: after a birth the holder leaves its saddle sideways and slides the starboard kit 50 mm along the rails into the pick pocket (on the timeline); for the third birth the print needle slides the port kit in the same way, its tip passing under the kits between the rails (216 check frames, deepest overlap 0.00 mm). Push force about 0.21 N (friction 0.3 on the kit weight in the gel plus the yield stress on its front face; estimate) of 4.9 N payload

Docking from behind with the full store: the tail, gel included (7.0 kg, 6.0 kg of buoyancy) presses on the tank floor with 10 N; at a friction of 0.3 on wet glass (estimate) it slides with a push of about 3 N, from outside the tank; the three disc magnets pull 161 N once the faces touch

Air: the inflator of the artist fills a size 7 basketball (7.6 L, 55 kPa) in 35 s, which is 7.1 L of free air per minute; the newborn (11.9 L at 1.6 kPa) fills in about 101 s. The inflator must stop at 1.6 kPa: the preset of a tire inflator may not go that low (open question)
Every pose of the timeline is inside the official joint ranges (base -40 to 40, J1 0 to 58, J2 1 to 85 degrees)

Electromagnet (Adafruit 3872, 2.5 kg holding force): lifting force taken as a tenth, 2.5 N, through the thin silicone over the steel disk; the kit weighs 1.16 N in air and about 0.28 N in the gel: margin 2.1 in air (reduced from 2 by the pocket on top of the kit; 1.5 is taken as enough, since in the gel the kit weighs much less)

Release in the gel: with the magnet off, the yield stress of the gel holds the seated kit with about 0.19 N; a remanent pull of 2 percent would be 0.05 N (estimate; a short reverse pulse makes the release certain)
The steel disk adds 2.5 g on top of the kit; the metacentric height stays 23 mm
Payload while carrying the kit: 201 g of 500 g
Force of the needle on the valve stays under the payload: peak 2.45 N of 4.91 N
The rubber ball valve grips the needle against the largest upward pull: 2.34 N of about 2 N (estimate, to bench test)
The front of the newborn is pushed through the mouth: in the middle of the push the axis of the body crosses the mouth 33 mm from its center; the mouth is 185 mm tall and 209 mm wide
Folds can be printed: story pitch 3.6 mm with one valley, pleat walls 7.1 mm apart at mid depth (limit: 1.2 mm wall plus 2 mm of gel)
Kresling stories are bistable with a barrier strain of 2.1 percent, far under the 25 percent stretch of the skin
Stretch 1.25 stays under the limit point of the membrane (1.38) and uses 4 percent of the 663 percent elongation at break
Full size 426 x 246 mm against the gel chamber 396 x 314 x 336 mm: 107 percent of the length, 78 percent of the width
The newborn floats upright: metacentric height 23 mm
Draft 28 mm; the jet of the pump lies under water. Thrust of the one pump 39 mN at full duty
The motion settles: pitch rate in the last three seconds under 0.01 degrees per second; deepest contact at the lip 0.00 mm
Per frame penetration test over 2429 frames: deepest overlap of any pair 0.77 mm (limit 1 mm)

Leaves partly filled: at 60 percent of the full gas volume (7.1 of 11.9 L, 365 x 210 mm) the section of the newborn in the mouth plane, when the needle lets go, has a radius of 44 mm against 92 mm of the half height of the mouth (margin 48 mm); full, the same section would be 111 mm

Grown beyond the printed full size: the silicone stretches on like a balloon to 1.66 times the unfolded size (printed full size 1.25), 566 x 328 mm, 28.0 L, 3.9 times the volume at the exit; past the limit point of the membrane (1.38) the pressure falls as the body inflates, so even growth is assumed, not modeled; 66 percent strain uses 10 percent of the 663 percent elongation at break
The newborn grows while swimming straight ahead (no turn, no drift); the nose stays 96 mm short of the front glass; the draft goes from 31 to 28 mm and the pitch from 5.2 to 6.1 degrees

Tank 1750 x 600 x 600 mm, made to order: 190 mm of water behind the tail tip once docked (120 mm at the start of the docking); the parent body (731 mm long, 336 mm tall) and the newborn (566 mm) fit the 1720 mm inner length; the newborn leaves the lip and swims 342 mm, the nose stops 96 mm short of the front glass

No trim pocket, no ballast. With the kit at the front end of its band the newborn floats 5.0 degrees nose up (kit in the middle of the band: 5.5; kit 137 mm further forward, where the folded body is too slender to hold the kit: -2.5). Level trim would need the kit beyond the nose

Release drawn, not simulated: at each step of a drawn forward motion the newborn takes its pose of least energy (weight against buoyancy in the gel and the water) with its lowest contact 3 mm clear of the floor, the ramp, the lower lip and its rim. It settles 36 mm onto the gel, then rests on the ramp and is carried up it: the tail end rises from 100 to 219 mm, then the body tips over the lower lip into the water (pitch -11 to 35 degrees). Only overlaps are checked, frame by frame (see Penetration); what drives the slide:

One smooth spindle across the seam: in plan the slope of the outline changes by 0.08 degrees at the docking plane and the outline is convex over the whole body (largest second difference of 3000 samples -3.5e-08 m); in side view the roof changes slope by 0.00 degrees at the plane and is convex
Air balance: 20.86 L of air at 20 C and 102.6 kPa (0.878 mol, 21.13 L of free air) fills the body from 7.1 to 28.0 L (grown size); the body stays at 673 to 1536 Pa over the water

Air pump (assumed catalogue class, not a cited product): 1.5 L per minute free flow and about 40 kPa capability, far above the body pressure of about 1.5 kPa; fill time 14 min; at an assumed 1.5 W, 1268 J (0.35 Wh), 19 percent of the kit battery (1.85 Wh). The intake must stay above the waterline

deriv.name: Newborn form
deriv.value: 426 mm long, 238 mm wide, 242 mm tall at the printed full size (grown further by the stretch, see Growth)
deriv.why: A round fish like body: fullest 32 percent of the length behind the nose, a round nose, a long fine taper to a soft end. The pleat model stays round in section; the fish cues are a smooth scaling of the coordinates of the stories along the axis after the unfolding (zero while folded, so the print and the kit packing do not change): the section narrows sideways over the rear third to 0.5 of its height at the tail end, a soft vertical tail edge; the forehead is 7 percent higher and the belly 7 percent flatter in front. The page also rounds the step between open and folded stories inward only and lets the upper half sag a little while the body is partly filled; both are drawn only, the overlap checks use the fuller body

deriv.name: Arm base
deriv.value: fixed, 147 mm behind the docking plane, on a 5 mm steel plate on the tail floor
deriv.why: The folded DexArm ends 50 mm behind the plane. The plane stands further ahead of the arm than earlier (103 mm): everything for the tools must be behind the plane, and with the gel now starting at the seam the two modules hang in front of the arm base, 40 degrees to each side, so the plane stands just ahead of their heads.

deriv.name: Why the tools hang in the gel
deriv.value: needle tip at most 18 mm high at 150 mm from the axis, 48 mm at 200 mm
deriv.why: The shoulder of the DexArm is 127 mm above its base and each link is 150 mm; J1 cannot lean back and J2 stops at 85 degrees, so close to the base the wrist is low. Two rear ends of the gel were calculated. (a) A rear wall of the head at the docking plane, dry seam: the wall could be only 17 mm tall for the print needle to pass (the gel is 100 mm deep); a needle short enough would put the module head in the gel; a lowered middle of the wall would let the gel out (the yield stress of the gel holds a step of about 2.5 mm). (b) No wall at the seam: the gel runs across the seam and ends at one ridge of the tail shell in front of the arm base; the seam is sealed by a cord; the stems of the tools hang in the gel and travel in the gel, and no tool crosses anything. (b) passes and is built. All tool hardware (saddles, module heads, kit store) stays behind the plane.

deriv.name: Gel
deriv.value: 3.57 L, flat surface at 100 mm, held by the shell alone
deriv.why: Below 105 mm the shell is only as wide as the gel needs: 96 mm wide in the head, around the folded print (90 mm), and up to 210 mm wide in the tail, where the stems of the two tools and the magnet swing. The gel starts at the ridge of the tail shell, 62 mm behind the seam (1.14 L of the gel lie in the tail), and reaches 349 mm into the head, to where the lower lip rises through the surface: 89 percent of the length of the head. No inner wall, no baffle, no block.

deriv.name: Printed newborn
deriv.value: 150 x 90 mm, folded, as near to the arm as the arm allows
deriv.why: Re-derived for the folded body: the print needle reaches every point of the body only from 220 mm from the arm axis on (tail tip), because the upper layers of the tail end (up to 97 mm high) need the wrist higher than the arm can hold it nearer; the tail tip is set 3 mm further, 223 mm from the axis, 76 mm ahead of the seam. The earlier figure was 206 mm for the bowl front of an earlier version; the limit for the body is 220 mm.

deriv.name: Lower lip
deriv.value: 161 mm long: level floor, then one long smooth rise to the lip 143 mm high
deriv.why: The lower line of the double wall head, taken over unchanged (its inner keel, quilt_page/calc/keel_inner.npz; same docking plane, same 154 mm half width and 330 mm roof, so no scaling). The floor stays level to 379 mm from the arm axis, under the nose of the folded print (7 mm of gel under it), then sweeps up in one curve; it passes the gel surface 349 mm ahead of the docking plane and meets the lip 43 mm above the gel and 52 mm above the water. The mouth is a bowl: the lip leans back into the oblique mouth plane with a rolled edge. The gel volume follows from this line (3.57 L).

deriv.name: Head
deriv.value: 396 x 314 x 336 mm outside, 24.5 L inside
deriv.why: The outline of the double wall head: the lower lip 393 mm ahead of the docking plane, the roof one gentle arch from the seam through the top of the mouth at 325 mm, the sides closing from the seam (308 mm wide) to the mouth (209 mm wide). The mouth is an oval of 185 x 209 mm leaning back 21.3 degrees. Longer than the 340 mm bed of the H2S: it needs a larger printer or a split, which is not shown. Inside the head: its own shell and three seat bumps.

deriv.name: Tail
deriv.value: 332 mm from the seam to the tip, 21.7 L, one print
deriv.why: Shorter than the head (393 mm) and rounded. In plan the whole body keeps one outline: widest at the docking plane (154 mm of half width), level there, then one convex curve to a blunt rounded end (a cosine to the power 0.5). Half width 135 mm at the arm axis, 75 mm 50 mm before the tip. Side view: roof level at 330 mm over the arm tower, then one convex arc to the tip 125 mm above the floor; the floor stays flat to 282 mm behind the seam and rises in one curve to the tip. The store behind the arm is cut to one birth so that it fits. The arm comes no nearer to the shell than 5 mm.

deriv.name: Tools, all in the tail
deriv.value: two saddles and the kit magazine, the foremost 4 mm behind the docking plane
deriv.why: The print needle hangs 40 degrees to port and the holder (electromagnet and ball needle) 40 degrees to starboard, both 155 mm from the arm axis, on ledges with two stops carried by a short bracket from the tail wall; their stems stand in the gel. The kits wait in the gel on two rails of the tail floor, in front of the arm. A module leaves its saddle sideways, toward the centerline, at the one height (110 mm under the head) the arm can hold at these radii; the holder turns onto the kit, the magnet lifts the kit, and the arm carries the kit forward through the gel to the print seat. The bare quick release comes up behind a module (38 mm of travel).

deriv.name: Docking
deriv.value: in the water, from behind, gel face to gel face; three magnets, the seam sealed by a cord
deriv.why: The tank is full and the gel is in from the first frame. Before docking each part holds its own gel at its open docking face: gel and water have nearly the same density (taken as 1000 and 998 kg per cubic meter), so the face is balanced up to the water; the water stands 0 mm under the gel level of 91 mm (no print yet, the kit in the tail), so the gel stands 0.0 mm above the water and loads its face with 1.8 Pa against an assumed yield stress of 25 Pa (Carbopol about 0.4 percent, to be measured; Bhattacharjee et al., Sci. Adv. 1, e1500655, 2015, give 9 Pa at 0.2 percent). The tail slides forward on the floor, 70 mm in all, the last 10 mm at 1 mm per second, so the water between the gel faces is squeezed up and out with a shear under half the yield stress, down to a film of about 0.11 mm (1 mL). Docked, the print raises the gel to 100 mm, 9 mm above the water; then the gel side of the seam is higher by 92 Pa at the floor, water cannot enter, and the gel does not pass a gap under 2.2 mm. Three DC2-N52 disc magnets hold 161 N. No trapped water, no gel filling stage.

deriv.name: Store
deriv.value: 1 birth per store, behind the arm
deriv.why: The shorter tail holds the store for one birth. Each limit on its own: kits 3, silicone 1, energy 1, gel 1. Two printed cartridges of 52 mm bore and 60 mm stroke lie across the tail, one above the other, for part A and part B (255 mL for 226 mL), a stepper and the gel reservoir (27 mL for 25 mL) beside the lower one; three 18650 cells (3S, 38 Wh for 23 Wh) and the Adafruit 3910 pump above, behind the turntable of the arm; the Raspberry Pi 5 and the inflator of the artist on top. The magazine in front of the arm still holds three kits; the silicone, the cells and the gel are refilled after each birth. The store weighs 0.38 kg full.

deriv.name: Kit magazine
deriv.value: three pockets in one row across the gel slot, on two rails
deriv.why: The pick pocket stays on the centerline in front of the arm, 111 mm from the axis. A side pocket each side, 50 mm off the centerline. A module leaving its saddle sideways pushes the next kit along the rails: after the first birth the holder (needle tip 55 mm high, the magnet 3 mm over the kit tops) slides the starboard kit in; before the third birth the print needle slides the port kit in, its tip passing under the kits between the two rails. Push force about 0.21 N (estimate).

deriv.name: Kit of the newborn
deriv.value: 46 x 46 x 53 mm, 118 g, 13 mm ahead of the middle of its band
deriv.why: One AITIAO 3 to 5 V micro submersible pump (42.6 x 23.9 x 22.7 mm, about 30 g), the CodeCell C6 Drive, the 500 mAh cell and the steel disk, cast in silicone. Trim without any added part: the center of gravity of the newborn lies 196 mm from the tail tip, the center of buoyancy 231 mm (only the wide belly is in the water), so the newborn floats nose up. Moving the kit forward helps a little: 5.5 degrees with the kit in the middle of the band, 6.5 degrees at the front end of the band (built), -2.5 degrees if the kit sat 137 mm further forward. The valve stays on the tail cap, where the arm can reach it.

deriv.name: Full size newborn
deriv.why: Unchanged. Unfolding at about 300 Pa (estimate), full at 1582 Pa.

deriv.name: Birth
deriv.why: After the drain the newborn floats in the gel. The arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises onto the lip, and pushes; the valve is held 339 mm from the arm axis, 172 mm high, 201 mm short of the end of the lip. Peak force on the valve 2.45 N of 4.91 N. The needle lets go, the holder goes down behind the tail end and pushes -12 mm further (0.00 N), to the nearly level part of the lip; there the tail end rests with 0.00 N, and the jet of the pump (39 mN) slides the newborn off against 0 mN of friction (coefficient 0.2, an estimate; the lip is wet with gel).

deriv.name: Water
deriv.value: 94 mm deep, from the first frame
deriv.why: Set by the gel: 1 mm under the gel level before docking (91 mm), so the open gel faces never lie under the water outside. The newborn draws 28 mm; the lip is 52 mm above the water, the ridge in front of the arm base 13 mm. Evaporation must be topped up to hold the level within about 1 mm.

deriv.name: Time
deriv.why: No gel filling: the gel is in from the start and the arm tops up 25 mL in 15 s; print 116 min for 121 m of bead at 20 mm per second, cure 75 min, air about 101 s for 11.9 L.

verdict.point: Shorter, rounded tail, one print, clear like the head; no drawn joint
verdict.why: Tail 332 mm from the seam to the tip, head 393 mm; 21.7 L. One outline with the rest of the body: slope change 0.08 degrees at the docking plane. Store for 1: kits 3, silicone 1, energy 1, gel 1. Tank 1750 mm long, 190 mm of water behind the tail; the newborn swims 342 mm.

verdict.point: Gel from the docking seam forward, held by the shell alone
verdict.why: 3.57 L. From the ridge of the tail shell 62 mm behind the seam to 349 mm ahead of the seam (89 percent of the head). No inner wall, no baffle, no ballast block. The seam carries a cord.

verdict.point: Head like the double wall head: long, the floor rising in one long curve to a high lower lip, bowl mouth
verdict.ok: yes; the head no longer prints in one piece on the H2S
verdict.why: Lip 393 mm ahead of the seam, 143 mm high; 161 mm of level floor and rise. Mouth 185 x 209 mm, leaning back 21.3 degrees. Head 396 x 314 x 336 mm.

verdict.point: Print inside the rear gel, as near as the arm allows
verdict.why: Tail tip of the print 223 mm from the arm axis (limit 220 mm), 76 mm ahead of the seam.

verdict.point: No trim pocket; trim by the place of the kit
verdict.ok: pocket removed; 5.0 degrees nose up remain
verdict.why: Kit moved to the front end of its band. 5.5 degrees with the kit in the middle, 6.5 at the front end, -2.5 if the kit sat 137 mm further forward; level is not reachable by moving the kit (center of gravity 196 mm, center of buoyancy 231 mm from the tail tip).

verdict.point: One spindle, widest and tallest at the seam, tapering in side view and in plan
verdict.why: One convex outline in plan across the seam, slope change 0.08 degrees at the docking plane. Tail 21.7 L, head 24.5 L. Half width 154 mm at the seam, 135 mm at the arm axis, 104 mm at the mouth.

verdict.point: All tool hardware behind the docking plane; docking from behind
verdict.why: Saddles and kit store end 4 mm behind the plane; the arm axis is now 147 mm behind the plane.

verdict.point: Release along the lip without a longer second push
verdict.why: Second push -12 mm. Then 0.00 N on the lip, friction 0 mN at 0.2, jet 39 mN.

verdict.point: Water and gel from the first frame; both parts rest on the floor in the water
verdict.why: Apart, with its own gel: tail 6.6 kg against 6.0 kg (0.00 kg of steel under the arm base beyond the 5 mm plate), head 4.22 kg against 2.76 kg, no ballast block. The gel stands 0.0 mm above the water at the open faces (1.8 Pa of 25 Pa); docking gel face to gel face leaves about 1 mL of water.

verdict.point: The newborn does not shrink; the pump of the artist
verdict.why: Full size 426 x 246 mm, 11.9 L; one AITIAO pump, kit 118 g, newborn 0.360 kg.

limits: Open: the release of the partly filled newborn is drawn, not simulated: the arm reaches only 224 mm from its axis, so the body is drawn sliding up the ramp of the floor (resting on it, 3 mm clear) and over the lower lip; what drives that slide is not modeled (a push from behind, or a top up that raises the water and the gel together toward the lip, are options to test). The rubber ball valve must grip the needle against the largest upward pull of the push (2.34 N against about 2 N, estimate): bench test.

The kit reload (a module pushing a kit 50 mm along two rails through the gel) and the bonded joint of the two tail prints (sealed, its lower part under water outside) need bench tests. The silicone cartridges, the gel reservoir, the pumps and the cells are separate parts seated in the rear print; their mounts are not in the STL files. The inflator stops with its own battery: whether one charge fills three newborns is not stated on its page.

Open points on the parts: a tire inflator may not stop as low as 1.3 kPa; the force of the electromagnet through the silicone skin and its release in the gel need a bench test; the product pages of the inflator, the stopcock and the ball valve were read by the artist and the coordinator, not opened from here.

Estimates, to measure: the mass of the DexArm (2.4 kg), the power of the DexArm while moving (12 W), the mass of the inflator, the flow of the AITIAO pump through a 3.5 mm nozzle (70 of its 100 L/h), the mass of the cast kit, the module head (30 x 40 x 52 mm), the seal of the cup, the flow of gel through a 3.5 mm tube, the pressure that opens the folds (300 Pa), the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), the pump curve of the kit pumps, friction at the lip (0.2).

How the official joint angles J1 and J2 map onto the link meshes is an assumption, as on the full version. The DexArm specification page was opened on 22 November 2026: 500 g payload (400 g in its Teach and Pneumatic section), 2.4 kg, joint ranges as used here, and a reach of 380 mm in the Teach and Pneumatic section. The reach here is not a fixed number: every pose is solved from the link lengths and the joint ranges; the longer stated reach changes nothing in this design.

The print path in the G-code is the smooth envelope of the folded body (47 m of bead); the pleat flanks between those contours are not drawn. Print time and silicone (121 m, 226 mL) are set by the whole skin: area times 1.2 mm wall, plus 8 percent.

Gel and water from the first frame: the open gel faces before docking, the squeeze film at docking and the softening of the gel face by diffusion are estimates and need a bench test; the yield stress of 25 Pa needs a Carbopol of about 0.4 percent, to be measured (Bhattacharjee et al. 2015 report 9 Pa at 0.2 percent).

The valve is a soft boss on the tail cap and the nozzle stays vertical while the body pitches by up to 53 degrees: this needs a bench test. So does the drain of the gel from the folds, and whether a fold packed this tightly prints and opens as drawn.
The force on the valve is a quasi static estimate from slices: weight, buoyancy in the gel and in the water, the lip with friction, yield drag.

The newborn is drawn rigid with one soft droop where the body leaves the opening; a real skin at 300 Pa also wrinkles. In the force estimate the unfolded part outside is limp at that droop: the lip, the hull front and the water carry that part, and the arm steers only the part still inside. Friction at the gel wet lip is taken as 0.2.
The swim is a straight run on one jet; the speed comes from an estimated flow through the nozzle. The page for the AITIAO pump is a reseller page for the pump class; no primary page exists.

In the mouth the order in which the segments open is scripted: the three slender tail stories first, each wide segment once past the lip. A real skin under one pressure opens everywhere at once and presses on the wall of the mouth; whether the body then slips out as drawn needs a bench test.
Overlap is measured from sampled points (4 to 11 mm apart) against exact surfaces, so a figure can be about 1 mm off.

read.birth_text: Quasi static estimate from slices. Peak 2.45 N; the payload of the DexArm is 4.91 N. The needle pushes forward and down; the gel carries the body inside, the lip and the water carry the body outside.
read.tank_text: The tank is a rimless low iron glass tank made to order, 1750 x 600 x 600 mm with 15 mm glass. The parent body, 731 mm long and 336 mm tall, stands on the floor with 190 mm of water behind the tail tip (120 mm at the start of the docking); 94 mm of water (83 L) leave the lip of the opening 52 mm above the water and give the newborn 802 mm of open water ahead. Filled as shown the tank weighs about 234 kg.
